addin.help.heading: Help
addin.help.searchPlaceholder: Search the help, e.g. text message or password
addin.help.intro: CloudShare sends large files securely: the file is stored in your Nextcloud and the recipients get a link to download it. The password comes separately – automatically, after you have sent the message.
addin.help.start.title: Getting started (only once)
addin.help.start.1: Open a new message and click “CloudShare” in the ribbon.
addin.help.start.2: Click “Connect to Nextcloud”. The sign-in opens in the browser – usually without typing anything.
addin.help.files.title: Sending large files
addin.help.files.1: Write your message as usual and attach the file – or drag the file onto the CloudShare pane.
addin.help.files.2: Every attachment is already ticked – untick what should go as a normal attachment. The “×” to the right of a file removes it from the message.
addin.help.files.4: Click “Insert file as link” at the bottom. The attachment is replaced by a download link. Every further link goes right below the last one inserted – wherever the cursor is.
addin.help.files.5: Send the message. Shortly afterwards the recipients get the password in a separate message.
addin.help.files.note: You neither have to note down the password nor send it yourself.
addin.help.files.labels: If a file is marked as sensitive in Microsoft 365 (e.g. “Confidential”), this shows under its name, and the message gets the same sensitivity when you insert it. For an encrypted file (lock) a note appears below the file list: recipients outside your organisation can usually not open it. It can only be inserted after “Send as a link anyway”. If you would rather not send it, click the “×” at the top right of the note – the file is removed from the message.
addin.help.password.title: Password and how it is sent
addin.help.password.random: “Random password”: CloudShare creates a secure password that is easy to read out. That is almost always the right choice. It is not shown here – if you do need it (e.g. on the phone), you find it after inserting under “History” → “Password”. There is only one password per message: after the first link “Same password as before” is selected and, under “Password to”, “Same recipients as before”; the other choices are greyed out. Further files, a confidential message or an upload link in the same message get the same password the same way – the recipients get it only once. If you remove all CloudShare links from the message, the choice is free again. With a proof of delivery this message takes only further files with a proof.
addin.help.password.own: “Own password”: if you have already agreed on a password with the recipients.
addin.help.password.none: “No password”: anyone who knows the link can download the file. Only for documents that may be public anyway.
addin.help.password.privacy: Always send personal or confidential data with a password.
addin.help.password.channel: Right below the password, “Password to” lets you choose who gets the password: the recipients of the message, another email address or – if set up – a phone number (mobile or landline) by text message. While you type the address or number, CloudShare suggests matching entries from your Outlook contacts (if allowed); pick one with the arrow keys and Enter or a click. The address book icon next to the field shows all your contacts A to Z to search and choose from. With a text message, link and password arrive on separate ways; that is the most secure. The choice applies to the next link. If several links share a password but have different ways, the password arrives once on each of them – for example as a message to the recipients and as a text message. The language of the link card, the password mail and the text message is set in the settings (“Language for the recipients”).
addin.help.password.validity: Under “Validity” you set how long the link works (with a password at most 30 days) and how long and how often the password can be fetched. The defaults usually fit.
addin.help.message.title: Confidential message
addin.help.message.text: For short confidential details such as access data: choose “Message” at the top, write the text and click “Insert confidential message”. The text is not in the email. The recipients open it through a link with the password; it is deleted when it expires. You find the message again in “History”: there you see the password, can send it again or revoke the message. Not even CloudShare can read the text itself.
addin.help.request.title: Receiving files from others
addin.help.request.text: Choose “Request” at the top and click “Insert upload link”. The recipients – for example citizens or partners – can upload files to you through it, very large ones too. The files end up in your Nextcloud. “History” shows how many have arrived; depending on the setup you also get an email as soon as new files are there.
addin.help.proof.title: Proof of delivery
addin.help.proof.text: If you may later have to show that and when recipients got something, switch on “Proof of delivery” below the password before you insert the files as a link – the switch exists for “Files” only. After the first link is inserted it is fixed for this message; the text below it then says why. CloudShare then records with date and time the sending of the message, the password, every access and every download, plus a fingerprint of each file – none of it can be changed afterwards. In “History” you open the proof as a PDF. A message with a proof of delivery takes only files with a proof – send a confidential message or an upload link in a message of its own.
addin.help.proof.recipient: For the recipients there is one more step: before opening for the first time they enter their email address and get a six-digit code by email – with a button “Confirm address” that fills it in; on the page they then only click “Confirm and open”. This only works with the address your message went to – not with a distribution list. The page names you as the sender and the file. The password goes out only after the confirmation – sending it again from “History” (“Send again to”) is possible only after that too and then reaches only recipients who confirmed.
addin.help.proof.find: Every proof of delivery – also for links that expired long ago – is in the account menu at the bottom left under “Proofs of delivery”. The magnifier at the top right searches by case number, subject, recipient or file name. Each entry looks like one in “History”: a click on the subject opens the sent message. The case number stands under the file name; the colour of the seal after it shows the state – grey sent, blue address confirmed, green fetched –, a click on it opens the PDF, which starts with the result at a glance. If nothing was fetched once half of the validity has passed, CloudShare reminds you once by email – you can switch that off under “Settings”.
addin.help.shares.title: History
addin.help.shares.text: “History” – in the account menu at the bottom left – shows every valid link and confidential message you sent; the magnifier at the top right searches by subject, file or recipient. Each entry shows at the top the subject of the message – a click opens it –, below it what went out – the file name, “File request” or “Confidential message” (the symbol on the left shows the kind), with a proof of delivery the seal after it –, when and to whom the message went – if the password went to the same addresses it says “message and password to …”, otherwise a line of its own “Password to …” (e.g. another address or a text message) – until when the link is valid (“Valid until …” with a calendar symbol, orange in its last two days) and whether it was downloaded. The list is always current: it reloads when you open it and when you come back to the pane. If you open a sent message and click “CloudShare” there, you see the links of that message right away. The symbols on the right:
addin.help.shares.password: Password – shows the password (hidden until you click the eye; “Copy” works while it is hidden) and sends it again, by email or text message (only for links with a password, until they expire). As when sending, CloudShare suggests your Outlook contacts while you type, and the address book symbol next to the field shows them all; with “Another email address” it goes to exactly one address – to several recipients with “Recipients of the message”.
addin.help.shares.insert: Insert – inserts the file as a new link into the message you are writing (only while writing a message).
addin.help.shares.proof: Proof – for messages sent with proof of delivery the tracking ID stands under the file name; the seal after it opens the proof of delivery as a PDF.
addin.help.shares.revoke: Revoke – blocks the link at once, for example if it went to the wrong person. Click a second time to confirm (“Sure?”).
addin.help.shares.account: At the bottom left is your Nextcloud account. A click on it opens a menu: your account and the storage at the top, below it “Open Nextcloud” (your Nextcloud in the browser), “History” (every valid link), “Proofs of delivery” (all your proofs of delivery, if set up), “Settings”, “Send feedback” (a problem or a suggestion to whoever looks after CloudShare, if set up), “Help” (this guide) and “Disconnect” – disconnecting needs a second click to be safe.
addin.help.shares.notices: Depending on the setup you also get an email as soon as a file was downloaded for the first time or new files arrived through an upload link – with a proof of delivery with the PDF attached, and a reminder if nothing was fetched by half of the validity. Whether you get these notifications is up to you in the settings.
addin.help.settings.title: Settings
addin.help.settings.open: Click your account at the bottom left and then “Settings” to open your personal settings. They apply to you on every computer.
addin.help.settings.channels: Under “More settings” – Send the password to: which ways you are offered when inserting and which one is already selected for a new message.
addin.help.settings.notices: Notifications: whether you get an email when a file was downloaded, when files arrived through an upload link, when a text message with the password could not be delivered – and, with a proof of delivery, a reminder if nothing was fetched by half of the validity.
addin.help.settings.language: Also under “More settings” – “CloudShare language”: as in Outlook or a fixed language. Below it “Language for the recipients”: the language the recipients get the link card, the password mail and the text message in – for every message; it cannot be changed when sending.
addin.help.settings.signature: Signature: ends every email CloudShare sends to your recipients (password, confirmation code of a proof of delivery), so they see who it comes from. You can copy your Outlook signature into it as text; an empty line starts a new paragraph. Without an own signature, your organisation's applies, filled with your profile data.
addin.help.settings.fixed: What your organisation decides – for example which countries text messages may go to and which phone numbers are blocked – cannot be changed here. Every change is saved at once; “Reset” (under “More settings”) brings back your organisation's defaults.
addin.help.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
addin.help.faq.noPassword.q: The recipients did not get a password.
addin.help.faq.noPassword.a: Open “History” in the account menu at the bottom left, click the key icon (“Password”) at the link and send it again. Also ask the recipients to look in their spam folder.
addin.help.faq.expired.a: Expired links are no longer listed in “History”. Attach the file again and insert it as a link – this creates a new link with a new password.
addin.help.faq.wrong.q: I sent the link to the wrong person.
addin.help.faq.wrong.a: Click the “Revoke” icon (crossed-out circle) at the link in “History” and confirm with “Sure?”. After that nobody can download the file any more.
addin.help.faq.unsent.a: The message with this link has not been sent yet – for example because you discarded the draft. So the password has not been sent either. If you still send the message, everything is fine. Otherwise CloudShare revokes the link itself after 7 days; the “Revoke” icon (crossed-out circle) does it right away. If it says “Password not sent yet.”, the link has already been downloaded – for example because you opened it yourself or sent the message from an Outlook without CloudShare. CloudShare then does not revoke it itself; if you no longer need it, revoke it.
addin.help.faq.sms.q: I received the message “Text message not sent” or “Text message not delivered”.
addin.help.faq.sms.a: The password was then not sent – not any other way either. Send it again with the key icon (“Password”), for example to a corrected number.
addin.help.faq.who.a: Only those who have the link and the password. The files are stored in your Nextcloud; once the link has expired they can no longer be downloaded.
addin.help.faq.send.q: Outlook points me to CloudShare when sending.
addin.help.faq.send.a: The attachments of the message are larger together than your organisation’s limit. Open CloudShare and insert the files as a link. Whether you may send the message as it is, your organisation decides.
addin.help.support: If you have questions or problems, please contact your IT support.

mail.proof.explanation: All times are server time ({zone}). Every entry contains the SHA-256 value of the one before: if an entry is changed or removed afterwards, the chain no longer fits. Downloads are reported by Nextcloud, accesses to the password and to confidential messages are counted by Vaultwarden. Recipients confirm their address with a code sent to that address; the IP address is the one they reached CloudShare from.
